single.epic_title: Protect Public API Capacity with Traffic Limits and Quotas

issues.title: Define public API traffic-control policies
issues.description: Specify client identity rules, rate-limit windows, endpoint throttling behavior, monthly quota semantics, response status codes, headers, and configurable defaults. Document how authenticated API keys and unidentified clients are handled so implementation teams can use a single enforcement contract.
issues.estimate_rationale: The main complexity is aligning rate, throttling, and quota semantics across public endpoints and client identity types.

issues.title: Add burst rate limiting to public endpoints
issues.description: Implement configurable short-window request rate limits for public API clients using the traffic-control policy. Reject requests that exceed the applicable limit without consuming additional backend capacity, and ensure enforcement works consistently across API instances.
issues.estimate_rationale: This requires distributed enforcement, client identification, configuration, and consistent behavior across public API instances.

issues.title: Add endpoint throttling for noisy integrations
issues.description: Implement endpoint-level throttling that limits concurrent or in-flight work and applies backpressure when an integration consumes excessive capacity. Configure the behavior for public endpoints so one integration cannot materially degrade latency or availability for other clients.
issues.estimate_rationale: The scope includes endpoint capacity controls, backpressure behavior, and safe handling of requests while capacity is exhausted.

issues.title: Enforce monthly request quotas per API key
issues.description: Track API-key request consumption over a calendar-month quota period, reject requests after the configured quota is exhausted, and reset usage automatically at the next monthly boundary. Make increments and quota checks atomic so concurrent requests cannot bypass the limit.
issues.estimate_rationale: Persistent usage tracking, atomic enforcement, monthly rollover behavior, and failure handling introduce significant storage and concurrency integration work.

issues.title: Expose standardized limit and quota responses
issues.description: Add consistent response headers and error payloads for rate-limited, throttled, and quota-exhausted requests, including applicable limits, remaining capacity, and reset timing. Align the responses with the policy defined for public API consumers.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work spans shared API response handling and integration with three enforcement paths, but does not require new limit algorithms.

issues.title: Add traffic-control metrics and alerts
issues.description: Instrument rate-limit rejections, throttled requests, quota consumption, quota exhaustion, and enforcement failures by endpoint and API key without exposing sensitive key material. Add dashboards or alerts for abnormal rejection rates and service-capacity risk.
issues.estimate_rationale: Observability requires coordinated metrics, aggregation dimensions, dashboards, and actionable alert thresholds across all enforcement mechanisms.

issues.title: Validate limits under distributed load
issues.description: Add automated integration and load tests covering burst limits, concurrent endpoint throttling, monthly quota rollover, concurrent quota consumption, multi-instance enforcement, and fail-safe behavior. Verify that compliant clients retain acceptable access while noisy clients are constrained.
issues.estimate_rationale: The test matrix must cover concurrency, distributed state, time-bound resets, and interactions between multiple traffic controls.

issues.title: Document public API limits and quotas
issues.description: Publish client-facing documentation for rate limits, throttling behavior, monthly API-key quotas, response headers, error handling, and reset timing. Include guidance for integrations to back off and avoid exhausting their quotas.
issues.estimate_rationale: Documentation must explain several related enforcement behaviors and provide actionable integration guidance.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: scores a 4 because it covers all aspects of the original proposal with appropriate detail; there's room for improvement in specifying how unidentified clients are handled beyond the basic requirement
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: scores a 5 as each issue is distinct and necessary, building logically on previous tasks without overlap or redundancy
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: scores a 4 because dependencies are mostly logical but the dependency of task [7] on task [5] could be questioned since load testing can often precede response standardization in real-world scenarios
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: scores a 5 as the estimates seem well-proportioned to the work described, acknowledging that some tasks (like defining policies) are smaller but appropriately scoped compared to more complex implementation stories

issues.description: Update invoice PDF retrieval to read from S3 when a migrated object is available and fall back to the on-premises file server when it is not. Preserve existing access behavior and instrument fallback usage so the remaining on-premises dependency can be tracked during migration.
issues.estimate_rationale: This requires integrating S3 lookup and on-premises fallback behavior into invoice retrieval while adding usage instrumentation.

issues.title: Build the invoice PDF migration and verification process
issues.description: Create a repeatable migration process that enumerates historical invoice PDFs, copies them to the designated S3 location, and verifies each object using checksums against the source file. Record per-file success, checksum mismatches, missing sources, transfer errors, and retry state for audit and remediation.
issues.estimate_rationale: The repeatable migration workflow spans inventory, transfer, checksum validation, retry handling, and auditable per-file outcomes.

issues.title: Prepare secure S3 storage and migration access
issues.description: Configure the target S3 bucket, object naming and metadata conventions, encryption, lifecycle settings as required, and least-privilege access for invoice retrieval and migration operations. Validate that application and migration identities can perform only the required reads and writes.
issues.estimate_rationale: Storage setup combines security, lifecycle, naming, metadata, and least-privilege validation across application and migration identities.

issues.title: Run and reconcile the historical invoice migration
issues.description: Execute the migration for the full historical invoice inventory after the fallback read path, migration process, and S3 access are ready. Reconcile source and destination counts, review checksum and transfer failures, retry recoverable items, and produce a completion report with unresolved exceptions.
issues.estimate_rationale: The full migration run requires operational execution, reconciliation, failure review, retries, and completion reporting.

issues.title: Monitor invoice reads and retire the fallback path
issues.description: Monitor S3 retrieval success, on-premises fallback usage, migration errors, and missing-object reports throughout the transition. Once all historical PDFs are verified in S3 and fallback usage is zero or explicitly accepted, document the cutover criteria and remove or disable the on-premises read path.
issues.estimate_rationale: This combines transition monitoring, validation of cutover criteria, and safely disabling the legacy read path.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: Weak: The plan addresses both major aspects of the proposal but lacks specific milestones for when tasks should be completed, which could impact project coordination.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: Strong: Each issue is distinct and necessary, with no apparent padding or unnecessary duplication. The tasks are clearly defined and scoped appropriately to the proposal requirements.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: Strong: Dependencies are logically set up, ensuring that critical tasks like setting up S3 storage (issue [4]) precede the migration process (issue [3]). The plan ensures that the fallback read path is in place before running the migration.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: Moderate: Most estimates seem proportionate to the work described. However, enabling the feature flag (1 pt) might be underestimated, as it involves verifying across multiple user segments and environments. The S3 fallback reads task (5 pts) is well estimated, considering the complexity of maintaining existing access behavior.

rows.challenge: Coverage: 'every table that holds personal data' implies discovery/audit work that a plan focused on the download button will skip entirely.

issues.title: Inventory personal-data sources
issues.description: Identify every database table, object store, and service that contains personal data associated with a user, including ownership keys and required export formats. Produce a maintained source-to-archive mapping that will serve as the completeness checklist for implementation and review.
issues.estimate_rationale: The scope depends on discovering and validating coverage across potentially many schemas and services.

issues.title: Implement export job generation
issues.description: Build a backend export workflow that gathers a user’s records from every source in the approved inventory and packages them into one downloadable archive with a clear, machine-readable file structure and metadata. The workflow should run asynchronously so large accounts do not depend on a single request timeout.
issues.estimate_rationale: This spans multi-source data access, archive creation, asynchronous processing, and handling of large exports.

issues.title: Secure export storage and download
issues.description: Store completed archives in protected, temporary storage and expose an authorized download mechanism that verifies the requesting user, limits archive lifetime, and prevents cross-account access. Add controls for repeated requests, failed jobs, and cleanup of expired or superseded archives.
issues.estimate_rationale: The main complexity is enforcing authorization, retention, cleanup, and secure delivery around generated files.

issues.title: Add export controls to Account Settings
issues.description: Add an Account Settings experience that lets users request an export, see whether it is queued, processing, ready, or failed, and download it when available. Explain what the archive contains and provide actionable feedback for unavailable or failed exports.
issues.estimate_rationale: The UI requires request handling, status polling or refresh behavior, download integration, and state-specific messaging.

issues.title: Validate export completeness and privacy
issues.description: Create automated and end-to-end tests that verify every inventoried personal-data source is included, records are scoped to the requesting user, archive contents are readable, and unauthorized downloads are rejected. Include representative large-account, missing-data, retry, and expiration scenarios.
issues.estimate_rationale: Coverage requires cross-source fixtures and security-focused integration tests in addition to normal workflow testing.

issues.title: Document export coverage and operations
issues.description: Document the archive format, included data sources, retention period, user-facing behavior, and operational procedures for monitoring or retrying failed exports. Keep the source inventory and compliance evidence aligned with the shipped implementation.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work is focused on consolidating implementation details and compliance evidence once the workflow is defined.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: math.max(3, 4) - The plan includes all necessary components to fulfill the original proposal's requirements, such as identifying data sources, implementing export functionality, ensuring security, user interface integration, validation, and documentation.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: math.max(3, 4) - The plan avoids redundancy; each task is distinct and necessary for the successful implementation of the personal-data export feature. There's no unnecessary repetition or padding of issues.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: math.max(3, 4) - Dependencies are logically set up, ensuring that tasks like inventory (1), implementation (2), security (3), UI integration (4), validation (5), and documentation (6) follow a sensible order. No task is dependent on one that should come after it.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: math.max(2, 3) - The estimates are generally reasonable for the tasks described, with appropriate point values assigned to more complex or critical tasks (8pts for implementation and validation). However, some tasks like documentation might be underestimated if they require significant detail.

issues.title: Inventory all personal-data sources
issues.description: Identify every database table, data store, and related system that holds personal data associated with user accounts, including ownership and export format requirements. Produce a maintained inventory and map each source to the fields and account identifiers needed for extraction.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work is primarily discovery and documentation across multiple data stores, with moderate complexity in mapping fields and account identifiers.

issues.title: Define the export archive contract
issues.description: Specify the archive structure, file formats, field naming, metadata, handling of missing or deleted records, and completion/error behavior for a complete user export. Base the contract on the personal-data inventory so every source has an explicit representation.
issues.estimate_rationale: Defining a complete archive contract requires resolving representation and error-handling details for every inventoried source.

issues.title: Build the complete export service
issues.description: Implement the backend workflow that gathers a user’s personal data from every inventoried source, produces the agreed archive format, and reports export status and failures. Ensure the workflow handles large accounts without incomplete archives and provides coverage checks against the source inventory.
issues.estimate_rationale: This is the largest effort because it spans multi-source extraction, archive generation, large-account processing, failure handling, and coverage validation.

issues.title: Secure archive storage and downloads
issues.description: Implement protected storage and download handling for generated archives, including authorization checks, limited archive lifetime, secure transport, and cleanup of expired files. Prevent users from accessing another account’s archive and avoid exposing export contents through logs or error responses.
issues.estimate_rationale: Secure storage and downloads combine authorization, lifecycle cleanup, transport security, and protections against data leakage.

issues.title: Add personal-data export to Account Settings
issues.description: Add an Account Settings flow that lets a user request an export, see its processing status, and download the completed archive. Present clear messaging for in-progress, successful, expired, and failed exports without exposing data before authorization succeeds.
issues.estimate_rationale: The Account Settings flow covers request, status, download, and user-facing state handling while integrating with the export backend.

issues.title: Verify export completeness and compliance
issues.description: Create automated and end-to-end tests that validate authorization, archive generation, every inventoried personal-data source, failure handling, expiration, and download behavior. Document the export process, source coverage, retention rules, and operational checks so Legal and support teams can verify GDPR portability requests are fulfilled.
issues.estimate_rationale: Verification must cover all data sources and end-to-end security, lifecycle, failure, and compliance documentation requirements.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: Weakness in ensuring all identified data stores are covered (5/5). The plan includes a task to inventory personal-data sources and another to build the export service based on this inventory, which should cover every table and data store as required by the proposal.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: The plan avoids redundancy (5/5). Each issue is distinct and necessary, with clear dependencies that logically build upon each other without unnecessary overlap or padding.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: Dependencies are well-defined and logical (5/5). The sequence of tasks from inventory to implementation ensures that each step is based on the completion of its prerequisites, such as defining the export contract before building the service.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: Estimates appear reasonable for the scope and complexity (4/5). The points assigned to tasks are proportionate to their described work, with more complex stories like building the complete export service receiving higher point values. However, a 13-point estimate for such a critical task might be slightly high.

rows.challenge: Coverage + ordering: schema change, three consumers, and a downstream job. Tests whether the plan notices the accounting export at all.

issues.title: Define currency-aware monetary data model
issues.description: Add currency fields and validation to orders, refunds, and subscriptions, retaining integer minor-unit amounts and explicitly defining how supported currencies and their minor-unit precision are represented. Document the rules for storing, displaying, and validating monetary values so all services use the same model.
issues.estimate_rationale: This spans three financial data models and requires agreement on currency precision and validation rules.

issues.title: Migrate existing financial records as USD
issues.description: Update existing orders, refunds, and subscriptions so their previously USD-denominated amounts have an explicit USD currency value. Make the migration safe to run on production-scale tables and verify that no monetary amounts are converted or changed.
issues.estimate_rationale: The main effort is a safe data migration across multiple potentially large tables with financial integrity checks.

issues.title: Add currency selection to checkout
issues.description: Allow customers to choose from the configured supported currencies during checkout and show prices using the selected currency's minor-unit rules. Ensure the selected currency and quoted amounts are validated and carried through checkout creation rather than inferred from display formatting.
issues.estimate_rationale: This requires coordinated checkout UI, pricing, validation, and API changes, with currency conversion or quote-source behavior needing integration.

issues.title: Persist currencies across orders, refunds, and subscriptions
issues.description: Update order creation, refund processing, and subscription creation or renewal flows to persist and honor the transaction currency and integer minor-unit amounts. Prevent cross-currency operations unless explicitly supported, and expose currency in the relevant APIs and customer-facing financial views.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work crosses several lifecycle flows and must preserve currency consistently through creation, updates, refunds, and renewals.

issues.title: Update accounting exports for multiple currencies
issues.description: Modify the accounting export job and its output contract so each exported order, refund, and subscription amount includes its currency and is not treated as USD by default. Preserve compatibility or provide a versioned export path for downstream consumers, and add reconciliation checks for mixed-currency batches.
issues.estimate_rationale: The scope includes export transformation, downstream compatibility decisions, and reconciliation behavior for mixed currencies.

issues.title: Verify multi-currency financial flows
issues.description: Add automated coverage for currency selection, minor-unit precision, USD migration behavior, order and refund consistency, subscription renewals, and accounting export output. Include edge cases such as unsupported currencies, zero-decimal currencies if enabled, and invalid cross-currency operations.
issues.estimate_rationale: Coverage must span multiple services and financial edge cases rather than a single isolated component.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: Includes all necessary tasks to fully implement multi-currency support without unnecessary padding.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: Each task is clearly defined with a specific focus, avoiding overlap and ensuring each part of the epic is covered only once.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: Dependencies are logically set up; later tasks depend on foundational changes being completed first. The plan follows a clear progression from data model to migration to user interaction.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: Estimates appear proportionate to the complexity of each task. For example, defining the data model and migrating existing records are appropriately weighted as significant tasks that require careful handling.

issues.title: Define supported currencies and money representation
issues.description: Document the supported currency set, minor-unit precision, rounding rules, conversion or pricing-source rules, and fallback behavior for unavailable currencies. Establish a shared money representation that distinguishes the numeric amount from its ISO currency code rather than treating every value as USD cents.
issues.estimate_rationale: Requires defining cross-cutting currency and precision rules plus a shared money model used by later work.

issues.title: Migrate monetary tables to store currency
issues.description: Update the orders, refunds, and subscriptions schema and data-access layers so each monetary amount is stored with its currency and appropriate minor-unit value. Backfill all existing records as USD using the current integer values, and add validation to prevent amounts from being persisted without a currency.
issues.estimate_rationale: Spans schema and data-access changes across three monetary domains, including safe USD backfill and validation.

issues.title: Add currency selection and localized checkout pricing
issues.description: Let customers choose an available checkout currency and display all checkout prices, totals, taxes, and discounts in that currency using the defined precision and rounding rules. Ensure the selected currency is carried through checkout creation and payment authorization, with a clear fallback when the currency is unavailable.
issues.estimate_rationale: Combines currency selection, localized pricing and rounding across checkout totals, taxes, discounts, and payment authorization.

issues.title: Persist order and payment amounts in transaction currency
issues.description: Update order creation and payment integration flows to persist the selected currency and exact minor-unit amounts for line items, totals, fees, taxes, and payment transactions. Ensure downstream order retrieval and customer-facing receipts do not silently convert or relabel amounts as USD.
issues.estimate_rationale: Requires coordinated changes to order, payment-provider, persistence, retrieval, and receipt flows for all monetary fields.

issues.title: Process refunds in the original currency
issues.description: Update refund validation, calculation, provider requests, and persistence to use the original order currency and its minor-unit precision. Prevent cross-currency refund requests and expose the refund currency consistently in operational and customer-facing responses.
issues.estimate_rationale: Updates refund calculations, provider requests, persistence, validation, and responses within the established currency model.

issues.title: Charge subscriptions in their configured currency
issues.description: Update subscription creation, renewal, invoice, and cancellation-related payment flows to retain and use the subscription's currency. Ensure recurring charges, stored prices, and subscription records remain consistent when currencies have different minor-unit exponents.
issues.estimate_rationale: Covers multiple subscription lifecycle flows and recurring payment behavior with currency-specific precision and stored pricing.

issues.title: Export accounting records with currency metadata
issues.description: Update the accounting export job and its output contract so every order, refund, and subscription-related monetary value includes its ISO currency and correct minor-unit amount. Preserve the existing USD export format where compatible, while preventing mixed-currency records from being aggregated as a single currency.
issues.estimate_rationale: Requires export contract and aggregation changes to include currency metadata while preserving compatible USD output.

issues.title: Verify multi-currency flows and migration compatibility
issues.description: Add automated coverage for supported currency precision, checkout totals, payment authorization, refunds, subscription renewals, accounting exports, and USD backfill behavior. Validate representative zero-, two-, and non-two-decimal currencies and confirm existing USD records and integrations continue to work.
issues.estimate_rationale: Needs broad automated and compatibility coverage across currency precisions, end-to-end payment flows, exports, and migration behavior.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: The plan covers all aspects of the original proposal, including checkout support, database changes, refunds, subscriptions, and accounting exports. It also goes into detail about specific tasks such as currency representation and migration, which are crucial for a successful implementation.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: Each task or story in the plan is distinct and necessary. There is no obvious overlap or redundancy that would suggest padding or lack of clarity in responsibilities.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: The dependencies are logically structured, with foundational tasks (like defining supported currencies and migrating database schemas) preceding more complex functionalities (such as processing refunds in the original currency). The plan ensures that each step builds upon the previous ones.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: The estimates seem proportionate to the complexity of the tasks. For instance, defining supported currencies and money representation is given a lower estimate (3 pts) compared to more complex tasks like migrating monetary tables (8 pts). The plan also includes verification steps with a reasonable estimate, indicating a thorough approach.
